newsitem.title: CHINA: China first-half trade surplus $17.77 bln.
newsitem.headline: China first-half trade surplus $17.77 bln.

text.p: China posted a trade surplus of $17.77 billion in the first half of the year, the official Xinhua news agency said on Monday.
The surplus compared with a $13.92 billion surplus in the January to May period this year and from an $876 million surplus for the January to June period of last year.
Note: Figures in billions of U.S. dollars.
China's exports classified as general trade reached $34.97 billion in the first half, up 33.1 percent from the year-ago period, accounting for 43.3 percent of overall exports, the news agency said.
Exports under processing trade reached $43.84 billion in the first half, up 21.3 percent from the same period last year, it said.
Exports by state-owned firms totalled $45.67 billion in the period, up 25.2 percent year-on-year, while imports of state firms reached $27.11 billion, down 5.6 percent, Xinhua said.
Exports of foreign-funded firms reached $32.95 billion in the first half, up 25.9 percent from a year ago, it said.
